The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about Chautauqua

What is the doh of Chautauqua?

In this version, in G major, doh is G. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Chautauqua start on?

It starts on d (G in G major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

What words can be sung to Chautauqua?

Chautauqua is in the metre 7.7.7.7.4 + i: lines of 7, 7, 7, 7, 4,, then, i syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Chautauqua in the public domain?

Yes. William Fiske Sherwin died in 1888; the tune was first published in 1877. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
